Blast Morphology Thaw Survival and Pregnancy Outcomes Report

Michael Whitehouse

2026-02-05

Executive Summary

This report presents analysis of blast morphology characteristics and their association with thaw survival and pregnancy outcomes for frozen embryo transfers (FET).

Key Findings:

  • Thaw survival rates analyzed by warming protocol (rapid vs. conventional), day number, expansion grade, ICM grade, trophectoderm grade, and biopsy count
  • Pregnancy outcomes examined for autologous euploid single embryo transfers
  • Multivariable logistic regression and GEE models identify independent predictors of success
  • Embryo ranking model predicts clinical implantation rates for all morphological combinations

Thaw Survival Analysis

Study Population

Thaw procedures included in this analysis:

  • Must be part of “EMBRYO TRANSFER” attempts
  • Must have corresponding cryopreservation procedure in EMR
  • Analyzed by thaw protocol, morphological characteristics, and biopsy count 
thaw_counts <- thaws |>
  summarise(
    embryos = n(),
    attempts = n_distinct(attempt_id),
    patients = n_distinct(patient_id)
  )

cat(sprintf("**Total: %d embryos from %d attempts across %d patients**\n\n", 
            thaw_counts$embryos, thaw_counts$attempts, thaw_counts$patients))

Total: 10898 embryos from 10327 attempts across 6965 patients

overall_survival <- thaws |>

Thaw Survival Model 

logistic_tidy <- broom::tidy(logistic_model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)", term != "factor(total_biopsy_count)2") |>
  mutate(
    term = stringr::str_replace_all(term, "factor\\(([^)]+)\\)", "\\1"),
    term = stringr::str_replace_all(term, "_", " "),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^(day number)(.+)$", "Day Number: \\2"),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^(expansion)(.+)$", "Expansion: \\2"),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^(icm grade)(.+)$", "ICM Grade: \\2"),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^(troph grade)(.+)$", "Troph Grade: \\2"),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^(rapid thaw)(.+)$", "Thaw: \\2"),
    term = stringr::str_replace(term, "^had biopsy(TRUE|Biopsied)$", "Biopsied"),
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    conf.low = round(conf.low, 3),
    conf.high = round(conf.high, 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = term))
logistic_survival_plot <- ggplot(logistic_tidy, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = kb_colors$kb_night) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted odds ratios for thaw survival (95% CI)",
    x = "Odds Ratio (95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Reference: Unbiopsied D5 4AA, Conventional Thaw Protocol"
  )

add_kb_logo(logistic_survival_plot)

logistic_summary <- format_model_summary(logistic_model, exponentiate = TRUE)

gt_model_summary(logistic_summary, "Logistic") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Model Summary: Thaw Survival Predictors")

Pregnancy Outcomes Analysis

Study Population

Transfers included in pregnancy outcomes analysis:

  • Autologous euploid single embryo transfers (SETs)
  • Exclude recent transfers without outcome data
  • Chemical pregnancy: include_in_bhcg_outcomes = TRUE
  • Clinical pregnancy: include_in_sac_fh_outcomes = TRUE

Models

  • Multivariable logistic regression to model independent effects on chemical pregnancy outcomes.

  • GEE model to account for within-patient correlation, i.e. to adjust confidence intervals for correlated outcomes for patients with multiple transfers.

Chemical and Clinical Pregnancy Model Comparison 

preg_model_comparison <- chemical_logit_summary |>
  select(term, chemical_estimate = estimate, chemical_conf.low = conf.low, chemical_conf.high = conf.high, chemical_p.value = p.value) |>
  left_join(
    clinical_logit_summary |>
      select(term, clinical_estimate = estimate, clinical_conf.low = conf.low, clinical_conf.high = conf.high, clinical_p.value = p.value),
    by = "term"
  ) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    chemical_estimate = round(chemical_estimate, 3),
    chemical_conf.low = round(chemical_conf.low, 3), 
    chemical_conf.high = round(chemical_conf.high, 3),
    clinical_estimate = round(clinical_estimate, 3),
    clinical_conf.low = round(clinical_conf.low, 3), 
    clinical_conf.high = round(clinical_conf.high, 3),
    diff_estimate = round(chemical_estimate - clinical_estimate, 3),
    diff_p.value = round(chemical_p.value - clinical_p.value, 3)
  ) |> 
  arrange(desc(abs(diff_estimate)))

gt::gt(preg_model_comparison) |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Model Comparison: Chemical vs Clinical Pregnancy (Logistic Regression)") |>
  gt::cols_label(
    term = "Term",
    chemical_estimate = "Chemical OR",
    chemical_conf.low = "Chemical 95% CI Lower",
    chemical_conf.high = "Chemical 95% CI Upper",
    chemical_p.value = "Chemical p-value",
    clinical_estimate = "Clinical OR",
    clinical_conf.low = "Clinical 95% CI Lower",
    clinical_conf.high = "Clinical 95% CI Upper",
    clinical_p.value = "Clinical p-value",
    diff_estimate = "Difference in OR",
    diff_p.value = "Difference in p-value"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(chemical_estimate, chemical_conf.low, chemical_conf.high,
                             clinical_estimate, clinical_conf.low, clinical_conf.high), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(chemical_p.value, clinical_p.value), decimals = 4) |>
  kb_gt_theme()

Embryo Ranking Model

Current Ranking Criteria

Currently we rank euploid embryos for transfer based on the following criteria, in order:

Select embryos based on sex, if selected in the cycle plan.
Select embryos frozen by Kindbody over embryos frozen by non-Kindbody laboratories.
Select embryos frozen on Day 5, before Day 6, before Day 7.
Select embryos based on Inner Cell Mass (ICM) grades: A, B, C (A, before B, before C).
Select embryos based on Trophectoderm grades: A, B, C (A, before B, before C)
Pick ICM before Trophectoderm (example: 4AB before 4BA).
Select embryos by expansion grade: 5 before 4 before 3, then 6.
Select ONCE Biopsied over Re-biopsied embryos.
Use earliest patient age at retrieval as a tie breaker if all other selection criteria are equal.
If all other selection criteria are identical, select the lowest numbered embryo.

Predicted Clinical Implantation Rates

Using a logistic regression model with day number, expansion, ICM grade, trophectoderm grade, and rebiopsy status, we can rank embryos by their predicted clinical implantation rates instead. 

ranking_plot <- plot_forest(ranking_model, "Adjusted odds ratios for clinical pregnancy (95% CI) - Ranking Model", order_by_estimate = TRUE)
add_kb_logo(ranking_plot)

ranking_summary <- format_model_summary(ranking_model, exponentiate = TRUE)

gt_model_summary(ranking_summary, "Ranking") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Model Summary: Embryo Ranking Model")

model_combinations <- expand_grid(
  day_number = levels(ranking_data$day_number),
  expansion = levels(ranking_data$expansion),
  icm_grade = levels(ranking_data$icm_grade),
  troph_grade = levels(ranking_data$troph_grade),
  rebiopsied = levels(ranking_data$rebiopsied)
) |>
  mutate(
    day_number = factor(day_number, levels = levels(ranking_data$day_number)),
    expansion = factor(expansion, levels = levels(ranking_data$expansion)),
    icm_grade = factor(icm_grade, levels = levels(ranking_data$icm_grade)),
    troph_grade = factor(troph_grade, levels = levels(ranking_data$troph_grade)),
    rebiopsied = factor(rebiopsied, levels = levels(ranking_data$rebiopsied))
  )

predictions <- predict(ranking_model, newdata = model_combinations, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)

predicted_rates <- model_combinations |>
  mutate(
    predicted_implantation_rate = plogis(predictions$fit),
    conf_low = plogis(predictions$fit - 1.96 * predictions$se.fit),
    conf_high = plogis(predictions$fit + 1.96 * predictions$se.fit),
    combined_grade = paste0("D", day_number, " ", expansion, icm_grade, troph_grade, 
                      ifelse(rebiopsied == "TRUE", " rebx", ""))
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(predicted_implantation_rate)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())

DT::datatable(
  predicted_rates,
  colnames = str_to_title(predicted_rates |> names() |> str_replace_all("_", " ")) |> 
    str_replace("Icm", "ICM") |> 
    str_replace("Conf (Low|High)", "95% CI \\1"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = kb_dt_theme(),
  style = "bootstrap"
) |>
  DT::formatPercentage(c("predicted_implantation_rate", "conf_low", "conf_high"), 1)

Heatmap of Predicted Implantation Rates 

heatmap_plot <- ggplot(predicted_rates, aes(x = paste0(icm_grade, troph_grade), 
                             y = paste0("D", day_number, " ", expansion))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = predicted_implantation_rate)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", predicted_implantation_rate * 100)), 
            size = 3, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~rebiopsied, labeller = labeller(rebiopsied = c("FALSE" = "Once-Biopsied", "TRUE" = "Re-Biopsied"))) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = kb_colors$kb_red, 
    mid = kb_colors$kb_yellow, 
    high = kb_colors$kb_green,
    midpoint = median(predicted_rates$predicted_implantation_rate),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Predicted\nImplantation\nRate"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Clinical Implantation Rates by Embryo Characteristics",
    x = "ICM + Troph Grade",
    y = "Day + Expansion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

add_kb_logo(heatmap_plot)

Conclusions

  1. Thaw Survival: Thaw survival is significantly associated with expansion grade and day number.
  2. Pregnancy Outcomes: Both chemical and clinical pregnancy rates vary by morphology and patient characteristics.
  3. Embryo Ranking: Model-predicted implantation rates may provide better embryo rankings than the rough grading system currently in use. We should discuss ways to validate this ranking model, ideally with prospective data, and consider integrating it into clinical decision-making.

Caveats

  • Retrospective analysis subject to selection biases
  • Limited sample sizes in certain morphological subgroups
  • Regression models assume independence of observations; GEE models help address this but have their own limitations
